metadata.coordinateReferenceSystem: WGS84 longitude, latitude in decimal degrees
metadata.referenceYearPolicy: Natural Earth source datasets do not establish one effective reference year; retrieval and review dates are not reference years.
metadata.identityPolicy: Permanent locally assigned river-, lake-, sea- and ocean- IDs distinguish feature kinds and remain stable if display names change. Retain this release and geometry version when publishing later content.
metadata.curationPolicy: A reviewed educational selection of recognizable, meaningful-scale features for both a world map and globe. This is not a complete hydrographic inventory, population ranking or authoritative definition of every named basin.
metadata.geometryPolicy: Pinned Natural Earth vector v5.1.2 GeoJSON. River targets combine the explicitly listed named river and lake-centerline segments without changing coordinates, adding tributaries, interpolating missing mouths or inventing extensions. Lake boundaries and holes are unchanged. Sea and ocean targets union their explicitly listed 1:10m marine-label regions, including constituent seas, gulfs, bays and channels; the source uses separate cells for these interior waters, so the parent label cell alone is not a complete basin. Each union is intersected with the actual 1:50m ocean mask and has the bundled countries.json land union subtracted. Offline overlay uses Shapely 2.1.2/GEOS with a 0.000001-degree precision grid (less than 0.1 m coordinate rounding); there is no further simplification. Nonpolygon overlay remnants are discarded and exterior rings are counterclockwise. Island holes and antimeridian splits are preserved. These are generalized educational basin extents, not maritime legal boundaries or measured current shorelines.
metadata.antimeridianPolicy: Source polygons remain split at -180/+180; island holes are retained. The Arctic polar closing edge runs along latitude 90, not through lower latitudes. River coordinates retain their source segments. Longitude wraps represent the same physical point.
metadata.relationshipPolicy: countryIds are explicit curated crossing or bordering relationships, not one owning country and not an exhaustive list of every island, tributary, basin country or coastal territory. They are reviewed against the pinned Natural Earth physical/admin-0 geography. Names, inclusion and relationships do not decide sovereignty. Antarctica is absent from the country catalogue, so Southern Ocean has no countryId. regions describe ANY geographic relationship: generally associated countries’ Natural Earth regions, with explicit physical-location relationships for transcontinental Russia/Baikal and oceans. Eastern Asia for Lake Baikal avoids falsely locating this lake in Europe.
metadata.factPolicy: Cards contain source-backed names, classifications, geographic relationships and explicit target coverage notes. No length, depth, area, population, superlative or change-over-time claims are supplied. The inland Caspian is intentionally not included rather than equating its name with the marine sea category.

tolerancePolicy.description: Zero distance inside a water polygon (excluding island holes); otherwise shortest geodesic distance to any river segment or water-polygon boundary. A 25 km map-scale selection tolerance is not a width, shoreline claim or country relationship.

metadata.oceanBoundaryPolicy: Named ocean targets include their constituent marginal seas and coastal waters rather than only the open-ocean label cells. Basin grouping is explicit editorial geography: the Atlantic includes the Caribbean, Mediterranean, Black and Baltic basins; the Arctic includes Hudson Bay and the Canadian Arctic channels; the Indian includes the Red Sea, Persian Gulf, Bay of Bengal and Australian northern/western marginal waters; the Pacific includes the East Indian archipelago seas and the Southern includes Antarctic marginal seas. Norwegian Sea, Greenland Sea and Davis Strait are shared Atlantic/Arctic transition waters and are accepted for either parent ocean. Source-defined entrance straits are retained; ocean naming and boundaries are conventional, not sovereignty claims.

properties.name: Nile
properties.highlight: The mapped main stem runs through Sudan and Egypt; separately named White Nile and Blue Nile tributaries are not part of this target.

properties.name: Amazon
properties.highlight: The mapped Amazonas main stem links the western Amazon region with Brazil; separately named tributaries are not part of this target.

properties.name: Danube
properties.highlight: The source labels its upper course Donau and its lower course Danube; both are one learning target.

properties.name: Mississippi
properties.highlight: The mapped main stem is in the United States; the separately named Missouri and Ohio tributaries are not part of this target.

properties.name: Yangtze
properties.highlight: The Jinsha, Chang Jiang and Yangtze source segments are grouped into one named-river target in China.

properties.name: Congo
properties.highlight: The mapped Congo and Lualaba source segments form one target; part of the lower river follows country borders.

properties.name: Lake Victoria
properties.highlight: Lake Victoria is shared by Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya. The source also records Nyanza as a name.

properties.name: Lake Superior
properties.highlight: Lake Superior is shared by Canada and the United States.

properties.name: Lake Baikal
properties.highlight: Lake Baikal is in Russia, in the Asian part of the country. Water-region filters include Eastern Asia rather than treating Russia as the lake’s owning region.

properties.name: Lake Tanganyika
properties.highlight: Lake Tanganyika borders Tanzania, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi and Zambia.

properties.name: Mediterranean Sea
properties.highlight: The Mediterranean connects southern Europe, northern Africa and western Asia. The mapped basin includes its constituent seas, coastal gulfs and the Strait of Gibraltar.

properties.name: Caribbean Sea
properties.highlight: The Caribbean Sea lies beside the Caribbean islands, Central America and northern South America. The mapped basin includes the Gulf of Honduras, Gulf of Urabá and Yucatan Channel.

properties.name: Red Sea
properties.highlight: The Red Sea separates northeastern Africa from the Arabian Peninsula. Its mapped basin includes the gulfs of Suez and Aqaba and the Bab el Mandeb entrance.

properties.name: Black Sea
properties.highlight: The Black Sea borders eastern Europe and western Asia. The connected Sea of Azov is included in this basin target; country relationships do not decide sovereignty.

properties.name: Baltic Sea
properties.highlight: The Baltic basin includes the gulfs of Bothnia, Finland and Riga, coastal lagoons and the Danish straits through the Kattegat.

properties.name: Pacific Ocean
properties.highlight: The North Pacific and South Pacific form one target spanning both sides of the antimeridian, including their mapped marginal seas and coastal waters.

properties.name: Atlantic Ocean
properties.highlight: The North Atlantic and South Atlantic form one target between the Americas, Europe and Africa, including connected marginal seas such as the Caribbean and Mediterranean.

properties.name: Indian Ocean
properties.highlight: The Indian Ocean basin includes the Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, Red Sea and other connected marginal waters between Africa, Asia and Australia.

properties.name: Arctic Ocean
properties.highlight: The Arctic Ocean basin includes the polar ocean, its marginal seas and the Canadian Arctic channels. Atlantic transition waters can belong to both basin targets.

properties.name: Southern Ocean
properties.highlight: The Southern Ocean surrounds Antarctica and includes its mapped marginal seas, such as the Ross and Weddell seas. Antarctica is outside the bundled country catalogue, so no artificial country owner is assigned.
